slice: A11/A12 close-out - physical stored-byte deletion after a Studio delete, and the delete half of playlist CRUD
verdict: CRT-01 and SOC-01 both flip to PASS. A Studio delete in real Chromium removed video 1's database rows and left all 20 of its stored objects on disk; the shipped media-GC collector, run destructively from the admin UI with the typed PURGE confirmation, deleted exactly those 20 and nothing else - the second video's 19 objects are byte-identical by sha256 before and after, and still serve. Playlist CRUD's delete half exists in both the API and the UI and was exercised three-actor in real Chromium and again over the API with readback: one item removed (order preserved), then the whole playlist deleted, 404 for C, U and anonymous after a hard reload, the three videos untouched. No code change was needed in any repo.

lab.topology: one origin - a pipe-only node proxy on 127.0.0.1:8099 that drops the client's Accept-Encoding, in front of `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3100 and vidra-core api on :8088; a second vidra-core process with VIDRA_ROLE=worker and no listener
lab.postgres: native PostgreSQL 16.15 on 55446 (-k /tmp/a11lab), fresh cluster, core schema 135
lab.redis: native redis on 56380 (db 0), flushed at start
lab.storage: STORAGE_BACKEND=local with STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT under the scratch tree - never a bucket. The owner's 2026-09-08 approval is for exactly this shape
lab.search: vidra-search was NOT run: playlists are not a search entity at all (zero 'playlist' hits across vidra-search internal/, migrations/ and api/), so there is no index for a playlist delete to drop out of
lab.browser: real Chromium (Playwright 1.62.1, playwright-core driven directly), separate browser contexts for creator C, other user U and anonymous, hard reload between states
lab.fixtures: four real ffmpeg clips (testsrc2/testsrc/smptebars plus a sine tone, H.264/AAC) and a generated 64x64 PNG playlist cover; video 1 = 626,130 bytes sha256 f2888ea549ec613b3c0ec09e4ee8427f3f3e69ff305c4610f9dd06080c3216db
lab.rate_limits: RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false, so this lab says nothing about the shipped limits
lab.transcode_floor: TRANSCODING_MIN_FREE_SCRATCH_MB=256 - this box had about 4 GiB free against the shipped 10 GiB floor, which would otherwise refuse every claim
lab.registration: REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true from boot in a throwaway cluster, for the owner plus two synthetic actors; nothing pre-existing was changed, so there was no closed setting to restore
lab.teardown: api, worker, the Next standalone server, the proxy, redis and postgres are all stopped and the cluster, storage root and fixtures deleted

how_it_is_run.scheduled: cmd/api/main.go runMediaGCWorker - started only when VIDRA_ROLE runs workers AND MEDIA_GC_ENABLED is true, leader-elected (a follower skips the tick and does not spend the dry run). Boot timer at +5 minutes, then a 24h ticker. Neither is configurable: the interval and first-sweep delay are Go constants, not env keys
how_it_is_run.on_demand: POST /api/v1/admin/media/gc with body {"dry_run": false}, behind requireAuth + requireRole(admin); the endpoint is mounted whatever MEDIA_GC_ENABLED says. The UI is /admin/media (AdminMediaView): Run dry run, then Purge N orphans, then type PURGE, then Confirm permanent purge
how_it_is_run.cli: none - the binary's subcommands are migrate up/version/force only

knobs.MEDIA_GC_ENABLED: true (boot-baked; governs the daily unattended sweep only, not the admin POST)
knobs.breaker_floor: 100 orphans - a hard-coded absolute floor below which the ratio breaker never fires. The lab sweep was 51 percent orphans, well over 25, and correctly did NOT trip because 20 is under 100
knobs.grace_period: there is none - no age or mtime threshold anywhere in internal/mediagc. An object is deletable the moment its last database reference disappears

safety_rails_observed.bucket_ownership: not-applicable - the local-disk backend is exempt BY DESIGN (mediagc.OwnershipNotApplicable.AllowsDelete() is true); no adoption was needed or performed
safety_rails_observed.storage_migration_interlock: wired and silent (no campaign); a failing check would have forced a dry run
safety_rails_observed.reference_mode_import_interlock: guards AdoptBucket only, and is irrelevant here on two counts - no import ran, and local disk never asks the ownership question. Stated rather than skipped

grace_window.answer: an in-flight playback or segment request during the grace window 404s; it does not serve. The bytes are on disk but unreachable - every delivery route resolves through the database rows the delete removed
grace_window.unattended_duration: no age grace; the delay is purely the sweep schedule. The first sweep after each boot is always a dry run, so the earliest unattended DELETE is about 24h after the worker process starts, and a worker restarted more often than every 24h never deletes on its own. An admin can collect immediately from /admin/media

findings: Local-disk purge leaves EMPTY DIRECTORIES behind: after the 20 objects went, four empty directories remained under the deleted video's id (captions/{id}, web-videos/{id}, streaming-playlists/{id}/360p, streaming-playlists/{id}/cmaf). No bytes and nothing reachable, and the concept does not exist on S3, where a key delete leaves nothing. Recorded, not fixed - the storage interface is key/value and adding directory pruning would put an rmdir race into the delete path for no user-visible gain

A media-GC sweep writes NO job_runs row. It is audited (audit_log action=admin.media.gc) and logged, but it is deliberately not a jobloop.Loop, so it cannot appear on the admin job surfaces. The success criterion's 'audit/job-run rows' is satisfied by the audit half only
The storage/GC dashboard is /admin/media, not /admin/system. /admin/system carries an 'Object storage' dependency row (NOT CONFIGURED on local disk) and no GC panel at all

There is no purge-ledger TABLE. internal/httpapi/media_purge.go is the CDN-edge invalidation seam plus a prose ledger of known-unpurged cases; with no CDN configured it is inert. Physical deletion is the collector's job alone, and nothing else in the product deletes a stored object on a video delete

The first sweep after each boot is always a dry run - a deliberate design (the code comment says so and the admin UI copy tells the operator). Its consequence is worth stating plainly: an install whose worker restarts more often than daily never collects unattended
Neither delete control in PlaylistDetailView has a confirmation step, while the Studio video delete and the GC purge both do
what_failed_first: The first browser run of the playlist timeline died on page.reload with waitUntil networkidle - the playlist page never reaches network idle (the video cards keep fetching). It had already issued the item DELETE, so the fixture was left at two items; it was restored (re-add plus PUT reorder back to video 2/3/4) and the whole timeline re-run end to end on domcontentloaded with explicit waits. Both C's and U's access tokens had also expired mid-lab (15-minute access JWTs) and were re-minted. An earlier caption upload used PUT /videos/{id}/captions/{lang} and got 405; the shipped route is POST /videos/{id}/captions with language and label form fields
